data.body:
Enforced verify-identity result for the publication hold (2026-11-18 PST, rebar-session-3d705fec, fix tame-melodious-veery on branch veery-verify-identity-perf, commit 6149d61c008, landing in progress).

Fresh no-remote TMPDIR clone of origin/tickets b878d77e28d; merged dry-run harness re-run with the fixed build: ok=true; commits 310,079 -> 12,675; blobless pack 625.0 MiB -> 99.3 MiB; reduced state equal; new tip fb999892b1e on a file:// fake remote only.

- ENFORCED `verify-identity --all` (no enforce_since), ORIGINAL history: completed in 27 min 1 s, **FAIL** — 42,612 verified / 874 unsigned / 7,007 bad-signature (50,493 in scope).
- ENFORCED, REWRITTEN history: completed in 20 min 40 s, **FAIL** — identical counts.

The runtime blocker is gone (previously >5.5 h without finishing). The hold's condition "enforced check PASSES on the rewritten history" is NOT met, but the cause predates the reclaim: the same 7,007 ledger entries fail on the original history. Filed starving-sphalerite-skua (df01-290f): ~4,987 ledger entries are signed by two keys not on identity 594c's keyring and ~1,320 have `signer_pubkey: null` recorded at compaction. Resolving it needs an operator decision (register keys, re-identify signers at verify time, or accept a grandfather boundary). Not filed as a reclaim defect, because the verdicts are identical before and after. Publication stays held; nothing was published, pushed, reset or force-updated.
